scope: Antisynthetase syndrome and its overlap with dermatomyositis and polymyositis.

keyRecommendations.text: Diagnosis is multidisciplinary, using rheumatology and pulmonary assessment plus serology, imaging, and sometimes muscle or lung biopsy.
ILD is more prevalent and more severe than in dermatomyositis and polymyositis.
Treatment choices are usually experiential because prospective data are lacking, and long-term care must watch immunosuppression and progressive ILD.

clinicalBottomLine: Antisynthetase syndrome is an inflammatory myopathy marked by antisynthetase antibodies and a high burden of interstitial lung disease, overlapping dermatomyositis and polymyositis but with more lung disease.
notableCaveats: Classic dermatomyositis skin signs other than mechanic's hands are not the focus, so they are not asked.
